plan.title: Liver RNA-seq: treated_a/treated_b vs control DE + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a 12,000 x 12 gene-level raw Salmon count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in column 1) with a 12-row sample table (metadata.csv) describing three groups — control, treated_a, treated_b — with 4 human liver replicates each, unpaired, single batch. The research question has two parts, and they need two different tests. 'Which genes differ across the three groups at all' is an omnibus question that spans two model coefficients, so it is answered by a DESeq2 likelihood ratio test of ~condition against ~1 — a Wald test on one coefficient cannot answer it. 'Which genes does each treatment change relative to control' is answered by named Wald contrasts (condition, treated_a, control) and (condition, treated_b, control), with control set as the explicit reference level so the sign of every fold change is unambiguous; the treated_b vs treated_a contrast is reported as a secondary comparison for readers asking whether the two treatments differ from each other. Because these contrasts are not all single coefficients, fold-change shrinkage uses ashr rather than apeglm. Multiple testing is BH at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering, adjusted within each contrast, and every gene list carries its contrast name. With 4 replicates per group DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cook's distance and returns NA p-values rather than replacing counts, so the number of NA genes from outlier flagging is reported separately from those dropped by the independent filter. Robustness is checked by re-running the same design through the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (omnibus F on both condition coefficients, plus per-contrast F tests) and reporting the intersection as the high-confidence set rather than the union. Interpretation is by fgsea preranked GSEA run once per contrast on the full ranked list of tested genes, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic — the disputed ranking-metric choice is settled on the Wald statistic because it scales effect by its uncertainty and does not saturate into ties; human MSigDB Hallmark is the first collection, Reactome the second. Note the matrix holds 12,000 gene symbols, well under a full human transcriptome, so it is already a reduced feature set; the tested-gene universe after filtering is what enrichment uses, and that limitation is stated in the report. Salmon length offsets are not recoverable from a pre-summarised gene-level CSV, so the model runs on the counts as given and the report states that the tximport length-offset route was unavailable.

Keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 4 samples (smallest group size)
~ condition with control set as explicit reference level; named contrasts treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control, plus treated_b vs treated_a
DESeq2 likelihood ratio test (~condition vs ~1) for any-difference, then pairwise Wald contrasts
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, alpha 0.05, within contrast
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic, per contrast, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
Consolidated report: design, thresholds, MA and dispersion plots, p-value histograms, shrunken and unshrunken LFC, leading-edge genes, edgeR QL overlap, session info

steps.name: Preranked GSEA per contrast (Hallmark, then Reactome)
steps.question: Which hallmark and Reactome pathways are coordinately shifted in treated_a vs control, in treated_b vs control, and in treated_b vs treated_a?
steps.description: For each of the three Wald contrast tables from T1S2, build a ranked list over ALL tested genes using the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the `stat` column) and run fgsea. This step needs two references, matched to Homo sapiens: the human MSigDB hallmark gene sets as the first collection, and the human Reactome pathway sets as the second — the Reactome GMT is multi-species and must be restricted to Homo sapiens via the pathway index before use. Both collections are in HGNC gene symbols, matching the counts matrix, so map identifiers only if a collection requires it and report the share of tested genes that fail to map. Restrict sets to 15-500 members after intersecting with the tested genes. Set and record the random seed for the permutation p-values. Collapse redundant significant sets (fgsea collapsePathways) and report one representative per group with the full table as a supplement. Write one table per contrast per collection, with the contrast named beside every set, and the leading-edge genes with their gene-level statistic for each significant set. Do not pool genes across contrasts. Also record the number of genes passing padj < 0.05 in each contrast; if fewer than about 50, note explicitly that no over-representation test was run and that the ranked method on the full list is the reason.
steps.context: Enrichment interpretation of three human liver contrasts. Ranking on the Wald statistic is a stated choice among the disputed alternatives: it scales the effect by its standard error and, unlike a signed p-value, does not produce ties at the top of the list when p-values saturate.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea run once per contrast on the FULL ranked list of tested genes — no significance or fold-change cutoff applied before ranking
Ranking metric is the DESeq2 Wald statistic, and the choice is stated in the output alongside the collection and its version
Human hallmark results written first, human Reactome results second, each as a separate per-contrast table
Reactome sets are confirmed restricted to Homo sapiens before testing, and the restriction is reported
Gene set size window 15-500 applied after intersection with the tested genes and reported
Random seed set and recorded; collection name and version recorded
Redundant significant sets collapsed, with one representative reported per group and the full table retained
Leading-edge genes listed per significant set with their gene-level statistic
If a required gene set collection is absent at run time, the step reports which one and completes with whichever collection is present rather than failing silently
constraints: Never threshold the gene list before ranking — GSEA takes every tested gene
Do not rank by the unshrunken log2 fold change alone, and do not rank by a signed p-value
Run enrichment once per contrast; do not pool genes from different contrasts into one list
Universe is the tested genes from T1S2, not the whole genome or the whole annotation
Use human gene sets only — the store also holds mouse and rat collections, and a species mismatch fails silently as an empty result rather than an error
BH-adjust the fgsea p-values within each contrast and each collection
caveats: The tested universe is at most 12,000 genes, smaller than a full human transcriptome, which shrinks set overlaps and must be stated with the results
Enrichment results are method-dependent; a significant set is a hypothesis for follow-up, not a proven mechanism
Reactome's `current` release is overwritten upstream each quarter — record the release/version actually used

steps.name: Consolidated report
steps.question: What is the consolidated, reproducible answer: how many genes differ across the three groups at all, what does each treatment change relative to control, and which pathways move?
steps.description: Assemble one report from T1S2, T1S3 and T2S1. State the method and every package version, the design formula ~ condition, the reference level control, each named contrast, the thresholds (padj < 0.05, BH, independent filtering on), the number of genes tested after filtering, and the number of significant genes for the LRT and for each contrast. Place the MA plot, the dispersion plot and the p-value histograms before the gene tables. Gene tables carry the unshrunken log2FoldChange, its lfcSE, and the ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange, ranked by the shrunken value, with the shrinkage estimator named in the header. Include the DESeq2 vs edgeR-QL overlap per comparison and mark the intersection as the high-confidence set. For the enrichment, report the collection and version, the Wald-statistic ranking metric, the tested-gene universe, the 15-500 size window, and the leading-edge genes per significant set, with the caveat that enrichment results depend on the method. Add a cross-contrast summary: genes significant in both treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control (shared treatment response), genes unique to one treatment, and the direction of change in each — presented as a description of overlap, not as a new test. Close with the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, seeds, package versions, gene set collection versions. State plainly that n=4 per group is small, that no batch or covariate information beyond condition exists in the metadata, and that the analysis is descriptive of these 12 liver samples.
steps.context: Final synthesis for the question 'which genes differ across the three groups at all, and which genes does each treatment change relative to control'. The LRT answers the first part, the two treatment-vs-control Wald contrasts the second.
acceptance_criteria: Report names the method, all package versions, the design formula, the reference level, and every contrast
Thresholds, number of genes tested after filtering, and number of significant genes per test are stated before the gene tables
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histograms appear before the gene tables with a description of what each shows
Gene tables give unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE and shrunken log2FoldChange, ranked by the shrunken value, estimator named
DESeq2 vs edgeR-QL counts and intersection reported per comparison, intersection labelled high-confidence
Enrichment section states database, version, ranking metric, universe and size window, and lists leading-edge genes per reported set
Cross-contrast overlap between treated_a vs control and treated_b vs control is described with directions, explicitly framed as descriptive overlap rather than a further test
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, seeds, package versions and collection versions is stored with the results
Limitations stated: n=4 per group, condition is the only covariate available, 12,000-gene reduced feature space, no tximport length offsets
constraints: Do not rank or headline genes by the unshrunken log2 fold change
Do not present the union of DESeq2 and edgeR calls as the result
Do not describe enrichment hits as established mechanisms
Report FDR control as holding within each contrast, not across the set of contrasts
Do not introduce any new statistical test at this step
caveats: Four replicates per group limits power; absence of a significant call is weak evidence of no effect
A gene significant in the LRT but in no pairwise contrast is a real pattern (diffuse difference), not an error
